dietEvidence.body: The skull is represented only by a maxilla fragment and a tooth. Herbivory is inferred from titanosaur anatomy; no gut contents are known, and the plants eaten cannot be identified.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A large titanosaur known from two partial skeletons with a relatively complete appendicular skeleton. The body mass is estimated from limb proportions.
summary: A large titanosaur known from two partial skeletons with a relatively complete appendicular skeleton. The body mass is estimated from limb proportions.

discovery.body: Named by Lacovara et al., 2014. The record is known from Cerro Fortaleza Formation, Santa Cruz. Two partial skeletons from the same locality, including a major part of the appendicular skeleton.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, MPM-PV 1156, is a partially articulated skeleton preserving much of the appendicular skeleton and tail; the paratype, MPM-PV 3546, is a smaller partial postcranial skeleton from the same locality.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Cerro Fortaleza Formation, Santa Cruz records the species in the Late Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈76–70 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The dorsal vertebrae are extensively pneumatised, the limb girdles are robust, and the tail includes 32 caudal vertebrae. The skull is represented by a maxilla fragment and a tooth.

behaviour.body: No direct evidence of social or parental behaviour. The two skeletons were buried together, but that is a taphonomic association, not proof that the animals lived as a herd.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from two partial skeletons from the same locality, including a major part of the appendicular skeleton. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The holotype, MPM-PV 1156, preserves about 45% of the skeleton, including much of the appendicular skeleton, pelvis, tail and a maxilla fragment; the paratype is MPM-PV 3546. The skull is almost unknown. Body mass is reconstructed from limb dimensions and body volume, and published estimates vary.

primer.lead: Dreadnoughtus schrani was a giant titanosaur from the [Late Cretaceous](/deep-time?period=cretaceous) of Patagonia. It is one of the most completely known giant sauropods, even though its skull is still almost unknown.
paragraphs: The holotype preserves about 45% of the skeleton, including much of the limbs, pelvis and tail. That is exceptional for a sauropod of this size, and it gives palaeontologists a detailed view of the appendicular anatomy. A second, smaller skeleton was found at the same site.

Body mass has been estimated in different ways, with published figures varying substantially. The animal was certainly enormous, but “22–38 tonnes” is a modelled range, not a reading from a scale. Its plant diet is inferred from other titanosaurs, and there is no direct evidence of its behaviour.
primer.takeaway: A giant known from an unusually complete body skeleton — but still without a usable skull.
